title: Module Overview: Cross Product-to-Sum via Paired Induction
content: This module proves the cross product-to-sum formula 2·T_m · U_n = U_{m+n} + U_{n-m} for Chebyshev polynomials. The T·T formula (from OQ-02) was 2·T_m·T_n = T_{m+n} + T_{m-n}; here the second factor is replaced by U_n of the second kind. The proof strategy is algebraic: prove the identity as a polynomial equation in R[X] for any CommRing R, then evaluate at cos θ. This avoids sin θ = 0 case analysis. The polynomial proof uses paired integer induction with invariant Q(m) = P(m) ∧ P(m-1).
mathContext: Open question from OQ-02: does $2T_m(x)T_n(x) = T_{m+n}(x) + T_{m-n}(x)$ extend to $U_n$? Answer: $2T_m(x) \cdot U_n(x) = U_{m+n}(x) + U_{n-m}(x)$.

title: Key Helper: 2·X·U_k = U_{k+1} + U_{k-1}
content: The private lemma `two_X_U` is the linchpin of the induction: it rearranges the U recurrence U_{k+2} = 2X·U_{k+1} - U_k as 2X·U_k = U_{k+1} + U_{k-1}. This is proved by `linear_combination -h` from the recurrence at k-1. The induction steps use this helper twice (once for U_{m+n} and once for U_{n-m}) to redistribute the 2X factor from the T recurrence. Without this helper the induction steps would require non-trivial manipulation of four U terms simultaneously.
mathContext: $2X \cdot U_k = U_{k+1} + U_{k-1}$: rearranges $U_{k+2} = 2X \cdot U_{k+1} - U_k$ with index shift $k \mapsto k-1$. Used as `two_X_U n k` in all three induction cases.

title: Paired Induction Invariant: Q(m) = P(m) ∧ P(m-1)
content: The induction invariant Q(m) carries both P(m): 2·T_m·U_n = U_{m+n}+U_{n-m} and P(m-1) simultaneously. This is necessary because the T recurrence T_{m+1} = 2X·T_m - T_{m-1} requires knowledge of both m and m-1. The base case Q(0) proves P(0) (from T_zero = 1) and P(-1) (T_{-1} = X, then use two_X_U). Integer induction via `Int.induction_on` then handles all m ∈ ℤ with forward step Q(m)→Q(m+1) and backward step Q(m)→Q(m-1). The main theorem `T_mul_U_product` extracts P(m) from Q(m).1.
mathContext: $Q(m) = P(m) \wedge P(m-1)$ where $P(m): 2T_m \cdot U_n = U_{m+n} + U_{n-m}$. Forward step uses $T_{m+1} = 2X \cdot T_m - T_{m-1}$; backward step uses $T_{m-2} = 2X \cdot T_{m-1} - T_m$.

title: Main Polynomial Identity: T_mul_U_product
content: T_mul_U_product states 2·T_m · U_n = U_{m+n} + U_{n-m} as a theorem in R[X] for any CommRing R and integers m, n. The proof extracts Q(m).1 via `suffices h : Q n m from h.1`. This is the most general form: it holds in any commutative ring (not just ℝ), making it applicable to formal Chebyshev series over arbitrary coefficient rings. The identity is asymmetric: U_{n-m} appears (not U_{m-n}), reflecting that U_{-k} ≠ U_k in general for the second-kind polynomials.
mathContext: $2T_m \cdot U_n = U_{m+n} + U_{n-m}$ in $R[X]$ for any `CommRing R` and $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Note asymmetry: $U_{n-m}$ not $U_{m-n}$ (since $U_{-k}(\cos\theta) = -U_{k-2}(\cos\theta)$ in general).

title: Real Form: Cross Product-to-Sum at cos θ
content: chebyshev_T_U_product_to_sum evaluates the polynomial identity at cos θ. The proof is a one-liner: apply T_mul_U_product (for R=ℝ), take congr_arg of eval at cos θ, then use simp to strip the Polynomial.eval wrapper and map_ofNat to handle the 2, then linarith. The key insight is that congr_arg converts a polynomial equality to a scalar equality, and simp normalizes the eval applications. No sin θ = 0 case analysis is needed because the polynomial proof already handled all cases.
mathContext: $2T_m(\cos\theta) \cdot U_n(\cos\theta) = U_{m+n}(\cos\theta) + U_{n-m}(\cos\theta)$ for all $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$, $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$. Proved by `congr_arg (Polynomial.eval (Real.cos θ))` on the polynomial identity.

title: U Recurrence at cos: chebyshev_cos_U
content: chebyshev_cos_U is the m=1 specialization: 2·cos θ·U_n(cos θ) = U_{n+1}(cos θ) + U_{n-1}(cos θ). This follows from chebyshev_T_U_product_to_sum with m=1, since T_1(cos θ) = cos θ (from T_real_cos at n=1: T_1(cos θ) = cos(1·θ) = cos θ). The convert tactic handles the cast arithmetic (1+n = n+1, n-1 = n-1). This recurrence at cos θ is the evaluation form of the polynomial recurrence U_{n+1} = 2X·U_n - U_{n-1}, rewritten as 2X·U_n = U_{n+1} + U_{n-1}.
mathContext: $2\cos\theta \cdot U_n(\cos\theta) = U_{n+1}(\cos\theta) + U_{n-1}(\cos\theta)$. Special case $m=1$ of the cross formula using $T_1(\cos\theta) = \cos\theta$.

title: Sine Spreading: 2·cos θ·sin((n+1)θ) = sin((n+2)θ) + sin(nθ)
content: two_cos_sin_spreading converts chebyshev_cos_U to trigonometric form using U_real_cos: U_n(cos θ)·sin θ = sin((n+1)θ). After substituting hcos (the U recurrence at cos), the proof rewrites U_{n+1} and U_{n-1} evaluations via their U_real_cos forms, adjusts cast arithmetic (hn1, hn2), then closes with nlinarith using sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and the commutativity of sin θ factors. This identity says cosine modulation maps a sine harmonic to neighboring harmonics — the sine analog of the cosine product formula.
